answer: The fable multiplier is published, charged in reef, and pearl lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 4 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3320 identities would post 3146 proofs and burn roughly 9 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
